items.title: Tele-Cranio: a CT-free AI solution for remote diagnosis and planning of craniomaxillofacial deformities
items.excerpt: Researchers built Tele-Cranio, an AI system that diagnoses craniomaxillofacial deformities and supports surgical planning remotely without in-hospital CT, aiming to cut repeat radiation exposure and access barriers, especially for children.

items.title: Cloud vs. on-premise large language models for urgent patient-portal message screening: a comparative evaluation
items.excerpt: Study tests whether LLMs can flag urgent concerns buried in rising patient-portal message volume, and whether locally hosted open-weight models can match cloud models for this outpatient triage task.

items.title: Harnessing smartwatches to spot undiagnosed hypertension
items.excerpt: With AI, a consumer smartwatch performed similarly to office-based hypertension measurement in a prospective clinical study, suggesting a route to population-level opportunistic screening for the roughly half of hypertensive adults who are undiagnosed.

items.title: RevealDx launches lung nodule viewer, AI monitoring dashboard
items.excerpt: RevealDx launched ReViewer, a diagnostic viewer that lets its FDA-cleared RevealAI-Lung nodule software run in any PACS, and ReViz, a dashboard for tracking AI performance; it plans to offer RevealAI-Screen lung cancer screening free to U.S. patients pending FDA clearance.

items.title: Mosaic Reporting tops 100K radiology reports a day
items.excerpt: Radiology Partners' AI-assisted Mosaic Reporting now handles more than 100,000 exams a day, about 75% of reports signed at its affiliated practices; 2,200+ radiologists across 74 practices have reported over 14 million exams on it.

items.title: Can AI refine body composition data gleaned from whole-body MRI?
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: a Prenuvo team applied an nnU-Net deep-learning model to 20,200 whole-body MRI scans to quantify visceral and subcutaneous fat and muscle, flagging metabolic syndrome risk without extra clinical workup.

items.title: Coreline Soft secures 13th FDA 510(k) clearance with aorta AI software
items.excerpt: Coreline Soft received FDA 510(k) clearance for AVIEW Aorta Metrics, AI software that measures aortic diameter on chest CT, bringing its total U.S. clearances to 13.

items.title: Lunit secures 11 oral presentation slots at RSNA 2026 with breast cancer AI research
items.excerpt: Lunit said 11 of its 17 AI medical-imaging abstracts were accepted as oral presentations at RSNA 2026; 15 focus on breast cancer detection and risk prediction.

items.title: The emerging winners and losers in the AI scribe market
items.excerpt: STAT's AI Prognosis looks at how the ambient AI scribe market is shaking out among health systems, with news from the HLTH conference.

items.title: Epic Systems defends competitive practices, promises to let AI access its records
items.excerpt: Epic executives at HLTH defended the EHR giant's competitive practices and pledged to let third-party AI tools access patient records held in its system.

items.title: Healthcare firms fail to monitor AI tools as shadow AI leads to breaches
items.excerpt: Healthcare organizations are adopting AI faster than their stretched security teams can monitor it, and unsanctioned 'shadow AI' use is already leading to data breaches.

items.title: AI is coming for primary care
items.excerpt: At HLTH, executives described AI moving into primary care, up to 'completely autonomous self-driving doctors'; Healthcare Dive asks whether the industry is ready.

items.title: AI imaging reports comparable to the work of sonographers and cardiologists
items.excerpt: In a randomized trial of AI- versus human-generated preliminary reports for 1,200 echocardiograms, blinded cardiologists edited 50.6% of AI reports and 49.7% of human reports, meeting noninferiority.

items.title: Voice changes may detect worsening heart failure weeks before other symptoms appear
items.excerpt: HearO records six spoken sentences daily on a smartphone; cloud AI builds a patient-specific voice model and alerts clinicians to acoustic changes signalling lung fluid build-up before heart failure worsens.

items.title: Patient info improperly used in radiology AI research, academic institution says
items.excerpt: Weill Cornell Medicine disclosed that individuals entered patient information from Weill Cornell Imaging at NewYork-Presbyterian into AI tools for machine-learning research without patient permission, violating its privacy policies.

items.title: Large language models show potential in MRI protocoling
items.excerpt: University Hospital Bonn researchers found some LLMs selected appropriate MRI protocols on par with radiologists, suggesting a way to standardize a largely manual, time-consuming task.

items.title: Medicare Pays For the AI Eye Scan — Nobody Pays For What Comes Next
items.excerpt: Medicare reimburses autonomous AI diabetic-retinopathy screening, but the follow-up care after a positive result is unfunded, which shapes every other barrier to deployment.

items.title: Recursion REC-4881 Phase 3 design aligned with FDA in FAP
items.excerpt: Recursion agreed with FDA on a registrational Phase 3 design for its AI-platform-derived MEK1/2 inhibitor REC-4881 in familial adenomatous polyposis, counting removal of adenomas 10 mm or larger as events; the ~200-patient trial is slated for H2 2027. (Off-list source: on-list outlets had no fresh coverage.)

items.title: Mental Health Needs and Emotional-Support Artificial Intelligence Use
items.excerpt: Cohort study in JAMA Network Open examines whether mental health needs are associated with regular use of emotional-support generative AI. (Date via Crossref created.)
